title: Vazrazhdane protest against the COVID-19 green certificate at the National Assembly
location: Square outside the National Assembly (Parliament), Sofia
scope: One public gathering at the National Assembly. The opened Sofia Globe report says protesters tried to force their way into the legislature. A Dir.bg search-only preview says the protest later moved to the Health Ministry; whether this was a connected movement or a separate gathering remains unresolved, so it is not merged here.
organizer: Vazrazhdane (as reported by the Sofia Globe; the BNT headline also attributes the protest to the party)
participants_original: The Sofia Globe reports “more than 1000” participants (opened article body); BTA’s search-only headline/preview reports “hundreds”; and BNR’s search-only preview says “thousands” participated. Keep each attributed; none gives an exact count.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened Sofia Globe report explicitly says more than 1,000 protesters; the BTA preview describes hundreds and BNR’s preview says thousands. These attributed reports support a crowd well above 50, but turnout differences remain unresolved and no numerical lower/upper bound is inferred from qualitative wording.

title.summary: The opened Sofia Globe article describes the green-certificate protest at Parliament on 12 January.

start_date.summary: Sofia Globe dates the protest to 12 January. The Sofia Municipality search result records traffic arrangements for a protest through 12 January; that notice is contextual and search-only.

end_date.summary: No source establishes the crowd’s physical closing time. The municipal traffic notice gives a scheduled restriction, while a Dir.bg search-only preview says the protest lasted more than six hours without a verified end time; end remains unknown.

location.summary: Sofia Globe locates the protest at Parliament; the municipal traffic notice is a search-only traffic record for the protest near Parliament.

scope.summary: Sofia Globe documents a crowd at Parliament. BNT search-only summary also mentions the Health Ministry, and a Dir.bg search-only preview says the protest moved there; whether the locations involve the same participants or a linked movement is unestablished, so no merge/split judgment is made.

organizer.summary: Sofia Globe says Vazrazhdane provided buses and its leader addressed the crowd by video; BNT headline names Vazrazhdane, and NOVA’s search-only title attributes organization to it.

demands.summary: The opened article identifies opposition to the green-certificate system; the BTA search result says the crowd demanded full repeal. Parliament’s 7 January search-only notice is policy context. Coded as social restrictions; exact demand wording is not independently body-checked.

participants.summary: Sofia Globe reports more than 1,000; BTA’s search-result preview says hundreds; BNR’s search-result preview says thousands. These are separately attributed qualitative reports, not a single agreed count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The opened Sofia Globe article reports more than 1,000; BTA search-only result reports hundreds, and BNR search-only result says thousands. These support at least 50 without an exact count or numeric bounds.

protester_violence.summary: Sofia Globe says protesters pushed back the police cordon to the building entrance and describes a struggle, but does not detail specific violence. BNT/ANSA/Rador search-only headlines mention clashes or injuries without body evidence. Keep protester violence unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Sofia Globe reports a conditional future offer by PM Petkov to receive a delegation after quarantine if protesters sent a qualified medical working group; it does not report an accepted or held meeting. A BTA search-only retrospective says a working group created after the protest met once and then ended over an online-broadcast dispute, but its participants/subject and relation to a protest delegation are unverified. Search-only Darik/Actualno headlines also suggest a health-minister interaction/MP meeting. Keep accommodation unknown.

state_response.arrests.summary: Sofia Globe says arrests of more aggressive protesters were made and separately reports police took a man with a firearm into custody; no arrest count is provided. Dir.bg’s search-only preview attributes detention of two demonstrators to MVR. The accounts are kept attributed and no combined total is inferred. Arrests coded yes.

state_response.beatings.summary: The opened Sofia Globe article reports four police injured in a struggle, but does not attribute beatings. ANSA/Rador injury headlines are search-only and do not identify the injured actors. Beatings remain unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The opened article describes a police cordon and internal barricading as protesters tried to enter Parliament, but does not report police attempting to disperse the gathering. Search-only headlines mention clashes/attempted entry. Do not treat police presence or blocking entry to the building as crowd dispersal; remain unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The opened article reports arrests and a conditional PM statement; BTA’s other search-only item concerns politicians’ comments. This evidence does not support an ignore code; leave unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: No death attributable to state force is reported in the opened article. Other injury headlines are search-only and do not establish a death; remain unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: The opened article mentions a man taken into custody with a firearm but no shooting by police; ANSA/Rador search-only injury headlines do not establish gunfire. Remain unknown.

open_questions: How do the BTA “hundreds,” Sofia Globe “more than 1000,” and BNR “thousands” descriptions relate, and what is the basis for each estimate?

Were any protesters injured? Sofia Globe reports four police officers hospitalized; Dir.bg search-only preview attributes nine police injuries to MVR and reports two demonstrators detained. Neither source establishes injuries to protesters, and the police counts/bases differ.
Did police attempt to disperse the crowd, or only hold the Parliament entrance? No dispersal action is identified in the opened article.
Was a formal meeting with a protest delegation agreed or held? The PM’s statement is conditional; health-minister meeting headlines and the BTA retrospective working-group preview remain search-only.
Were participants at the Health Ministry part of this Parliament gathering or a distinct group?
When did the gathering physically end? Dir.bg’s search-only preview says it lasted more than six hours but gives no verified closing time.
Is there any established cross-month continuation? None is assigned from this pass.
notes: One candidate for the 12 January Parliament gathering. Reported protester actions, police responses, injuries to police, possible injuries to protesters, and possible dialogue are kept separate. Sofia Globe’s opened body reports four police officers hospitalized after injuries in a struggle; the Dir.bg search-only preview attributes nine police injuries to MVR and says two demonstrators were detained, not injured. These different police counts remain attributed; neither source establishes injuries to demonstrators. The opened source describes protesters pushing the cordon but does not establish additional specific violence. Search-only reports remain leads. The conditional future offer by PM Petkov and later BTA working-group preview do not establish an agreed or completed delegation meeting. Reuters at Investing.com is one Reuters editorial origin, not two sources; multiple BNT/BTA/Darik articles are not treated as independent outlets. No link is inferred to the later February anti-certificate demonstration or to the uncertain 19 January education-strike lead.
